introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II, answer all questions choosing EITHER parts a, b and c OR parts d, e and f of each question. For your guidance, the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 1 shows a circuit diagram used to run a small radio from the mains transformer:

![fig-1](gce-ol-physics-2019-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)

(i) What kind of transformer is used? Explain. *[2 marks]*

(ii) Identify the component, M, and state its function. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) It is a **step-down transformer**. The mains supply is $240\,\mathrm{V}$ but a small radio needs a much lower voltage. In Figure 1 the primary coil (connected to the mains) has **more turns** than the secondary coil (connected to the radio), and $\dfrac{V_s}{V_p} = \dfrac{N_s}{N_p} < 1$, so the output voltage is smaller than the input voltage.

(ii) M is a **(semiconductor) diode**. It allows current to flow in **one direction only**, so it **rectifies** the alternating current from the secondary coil into direct current (d.c.) suitable for the radio.

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 2 shows a solenoid wound on a cardboard tube. The ends of the solenoid are connected to a DC source through a rheostat and switch.

![fig-2](gce-ol-physics-2019-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)

(i) Copy the figure and sketch the magnetic field (indicating its polarity) when the switch is closed. *[2 marks]*

(ii) State one method of making the magnetic field stronger. *[1 mark]*

(iii) Name one device which makes use of magnetism that can be switched on and off. *[1 mark]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **Sketch:** copy the solenoid and the circuit. Inside the solenoid draw several **straight, parallel field lines** along the axis, close together and evenly spaced. Outside, draw lines that leave one end, curve round and enter the other end, exactly like the field of a **bar magnet**. Put arrowheads on the lines: they point **out of the north pole, round the outside, and into the south pole** (and along the axis from south to north inside the coil).

**Polarity:** the cell has its positive terminal (the longer line) on the left, so conventional current flows up the left wire into the left end of the coil and runs down the front of the turns as drawn. By the right-hand grip rule (fingers along the current, thumb gives the north pole), the **right-hand end is the north pole** and the **left-hand end is the south pole**. (If the cell were reversed, the two poles would swap.)

(ii) Any one: **increase the current** (reduce the resistance of the rheostat or use a larger e.m.f.); **increase the number of turns** per unit length; **insert a soft-iron core** inside the solenoid.

(iii) An **electromagnet** based device, for example an **electric bell**, a **relay**, a **circuit breaker**, a **loudspeaker** or a scrap-yard crane (any one).
